content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations using the elimination method.

answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by 4 and the second by 5:
$$\begin{align*}8x+20y&=48\\15x-20y&=-25\end{align*}$$
Add:
$$\begin{align*}(8x+20y)+(15x-20y)&=48-25\\23x&=23\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(1)+5y&=12\\5y&=10\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(1)+5(2)=12$ and $3(1)-4(2)=-5$.

Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2:
$$\begin{align*}9x-6y&=51\\8x+6y&=0\end{align*}$$
Add:
$$\begin{align*}(9x-6y)+(8x+6y)&=51+0\\17x&=51\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}3(3)-2y&=17\\-2y&=8\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
Check: $3(3)-2(-4)=17$ and $4(3)+3(-4)=0$.

Multiply the first equation by 4 and the second by 3:
$$\begin{align*}8x+12y&=-16\\15x+12y&=-9\end{align*}$$
Subtract the first resulting equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}(15x+12y)-(8x+12y)&=-9-(-16)\\7x&=7\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first original equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(1)+3y&=-4\\3y&=-6\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(1)+3(-2)=-4$ and $5(1)+4(-2)=-3$.

$x=\dfrac{103}{11},\ y=\dfrac{108}{11}$.

Multiply both equations to eliminate $y$, then substitute to find $y$.
answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5:
$$\begin{align*}9x-15y&=-63\\20x-15y&=40\end{align*}$$
Subtract the first resulting equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}(20x-15y)-(9x-15y)&=40-(-63)\\11x&=103\\x&=\frac{103}{11}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the second original equation:
$$\begin{align*}4\left(\frac{103}{11}\right)-3y&=8\\-3y&=\frac{88}{11}-\frac{412}{11}\\-3y&=-\frac{324}{11}\\y&=\frac{108}{11}\end{align*}$$
Check:
$$\begin{align*}3\left(\frac{103}{11}\right)-5\left(\frac{108}{11}\right)&=-21\\4\left(\frac{103}{11}\right)-3\left(\frac{108}{11}\right)&=8\end{align*}$$
